nodes.title: Potentially semistable point sets
nodes.statement: Let F/Q_p be finite, d≥1, L/Q_p a sufficiently large finite coefficient field with integers O and residue k, and ρ̄:G_F→GL_d(k) continuous, with absolutely irreducible Jordan–Hölder factors after the allowed coefficient enlargement. Put R=R□_{ρ̄} and X=Spec R. Points mean kernels of O-algebra maps R→L′ for finite L′/L, equivalently closed points of Spec R[1/p], mapped into X. Label Hodge–Tate weights decreasingly, k_{σ,1}>⋯>k_{σ,d}; use HT(ε)=−1. Σcris consists of crystalline points of any regular labelled weight. Σ_k consists of potentially semistable points of the fixed regular weight k. Σprnc_k is its potentially crystabelline subset (crystalline after a finite abelian extension). Σspcd_k consists of those x∈Σ_k with N=0 and WD(ρ_x) irreducible, induced from a character of the Weil group of the unramified degree-d extension. Local Langlands uses CEGGPS r_p(π)=rec_p(π⊗|det|^{(1−d)/2}), with geometric Artin reciprocity. The algebraic test representation is πalg(ρ)=L_a^d⊗L for a_{σ,i}=k_{σ,i}−(d−i); thus its highest weight is −a_{σ,d+1−i}.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Use the local lifting-ring point functor, then define the subsets by the stated p-adic Hodge and Weil–Deligne conditions.
Read weights through CEGGPS §1.8: the lattice L_a is dualised in πalg. Compare DPS Remark 5.14 only after reversing its HT(ε)=+1 convention.
Factor out embeddings of residue fields: changing a field of definition preserves the underlying prime and the predicates.
acceptance: For d=2 and weights (1,0), a=(0,0) and πalg is trivial.
The fixed-weight density conclusion is made in Spec R; it is not a claim about the rigid generic fibre.

Hence R∞ is reduced, O-flat and flat over R□_{ρ̄}. After finite coefficient enlargement making each A/𝔭 geometrically integral, its minimal primes are indexed bijectively by (χ,𝔭), where χ:μ_{p∞}(F)→O× and 𝔭∈Min(A). The associated component ring is R□,χ_{ρ̄}⊗̂_O A/𝔭; distinct pairs are distinct and contraction to R□_{ρ̄} is its χ-component prime. Here R□,χ fixes the determinant on μ_{p∞}(F), not the whole determinant.

nodes.title: Roots of torsion-free characters
nodes.statement: If ψ:G_F→O× is continuous and trivial on the torsion subgroup of G_F^ab, then for every integer d≥1 there is, after a finite extension L′/L, a continuous η:G_F→O_{L′}× with η^d=ψ. No assumption p∤2d is used in this lemma.
hypotheses: F/Q_p finite; d≥1; ψ continuous and trivial on torsion.
proofSteps: Use the torsion-free quotient G_F^ab/tors≅Ẑ×Z_p^{[F:Q_p]}. Split off an unramified Teichmüller character whose d-th power matches the residue on the Ẑ generator.

The remaining character factors through Z_p^{[F:Q_p]+1} with principal-unit values. Choose finitely many d-th roots 1+y_i after one finite coefficient extension, and use the convergent binomial powers (1+y_i)^x for x∈Z_p.
Multiply by the Teichmüller root and inflate. The torsion hypothesis is what makes the quotient construction possible.
acceptance: d=1 gives η=ψ.
The identity character on a finite torsion subgroup need not admit a compatible d-th root; the quotient hypothesis cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: Algebraic central character
nodes.statement: Let ψ:G_F→O× be a crystalline lift of detρ̄ and xψ:R_{detρ̄}→O. On Mψ=M∞⊗̂_{R_{detρ̄},xψ}O, the centre acts by δ^{-1}, where δ=(ε^{d(d−1)/2}ψ)∘Art_F for geometric Art_F. The parent supplies that Mψ is nonzero projective in the compact fixed-central-character category. The restriction δ|_{Z∩K}, identified on O_F×, is the evaluation of an algebraic character θ of (Res_{F/Q_p}G_m)_L. The sign of θ is obtained by converting the arithmetic reciprocity convention of R06.2 to geometric reciprocity.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Use parent central projectivity, CEGGPS §4.22 and Corollary 4.26; do not reconstruct the fixed-centre module.
The product ε^{d(d−1)/2}ψ is crystalline. Apply the rank-one crystalline classification to its restriction through the geometric Artin map, obtained by inversion from the supplied arithmetic map.
The algebraic exponents determine θ. Keep the inverse on Mψ and δ on its contragredient Banach dual.
acceptance: For d=1 and ψ=1, δ=1; both module and Banach central characters are trivial.
Contragredient duality changes δ^{-1} to δ.

nodes.title: Capture
nodes.statement: For a compact group H with an open pro-p subgroup, compact linear-topological O[[H]]-module M, and finite-dimensional continuous L-representations (V_i) of H, the family captures M when the intersection of the kernels of all continuous O[[H]]-linear maps M→V_i* is zero. The dual V_i* is the L-linear contragredient, restricted to O; no finite-generation assumption on M is part of this definition.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Define the closed common kernel using continuous equivariant maps, and compare with the smallest quotient preserving all Hom spaces.
Schikhof duality on O-torsion-free modules identifies capture with density of the evaluation map into Π(M). Any O-torsion lies in every kernel.
Products are captured exactly when their factors are, and capture of O[[H]] is equivalent to capture of every compact projective, using products of indecomposable projectives.
acceptance: Continuous maps, rather than arbitrary algebraic maps, are required.
The characterization must apply to projectives that are not finite over O[[H]].

nodes.title: Scalar detection by testing kernels
nodes.statement: Let O and R be commutative rings, M an O-module and an R-module with faithful R-action, and (f_i:M→V_i) an indexed family of O-linear maps to O-modules. If ⋂_i ker f_i=0, then any R-scalar a with f_i(a·m)=0 for every i,m is zero. More generally any O-linear endomorphism u with f_i∘u=0 for every i is zero. Applied to all continuous equivariant maps to V_i*, this is the scalar-detection consequence of capture.
hypotheses: The hypotheses in the statement; arithmetic specialisations use the PD.0 setup.
proofSteps: For each m, every f_i kills u(m) or a·m, so the common-kernel hypothesis makes it zero.
Extensionality gives u=0; faithful scalar action compares a with zero to give a=0.
acceptance: The statement uses continuous compact duality only under O-torsion-freeness.
The algebraic kernel form does not replace a missing representation carrier.

nodes.title: Patched testing modules
nodes.statement: For a compact open H⊆K, finite-dimensional continuous H-representation V over L and H-stable O-lattice Θ, extend the parent testing construction to M∞,H(Θ)=(Hom_cont,O[[H]](M∞,Θ^d))^d, using Schikhof duals. This is a finite R∞-module. Its rational version M∞,H(V)=M∞,H(Θ)[1/p] is canonically independent of Θ. It is contravariantly tested against V* and its continuous L-linear dual is Hom_H(V,Π(M∞)); scalar actions are by precomposition. For σ=πalg(k)⊗σ(τ) at H=K this is the existing parent type-specialised module, not a new type-theory object.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Restrict the finite R∞[[K]] presentation to H, which has finite index, so it remains finite over R∞[[H]]. The right Θ-module uses g↦g^{-1}.
Identify the displayed double dual with the completed balanced tensor Θ⊗̂_{O[[H]]}M∞. A finite presentation makes it a quotient of finitely many copies of R∞⊗_OΘ, proving finiteness.
Compare commensurable lattices after inverting p and use torsion-free biduality for the Hom adjunction. Frobenius reciprocity compares H-tests with induced K-tests.
Use the imported parent theorem, rather than general finiteness, to obtain reduced O-flat faithful quotients for algebraic and type-specialised tests.
acceptance: M∞ need not be finite as an R∞-module or as an O[[H]]-module.
Reducedness of the testing quotient is an arithmetic theorem, not a consequence of this definition.

nodes.title: Algebraic capture
nodes.statement: For K=GL_d(O_F), irreducible rational representations ξ of (Res_{F/Q_p}GL_d)_L capture every compact projective O[[K]]-module. If a family captures every compact projective for a compact H, tensoring every member with a fixed nonzero finite-dimensional continuous H-representation W still captures every compact projective. In particular {ξ⊗W}_ξ captures all K-projectives for any nonzero finite-dimensional smooth K-representation W. Finite fields of definition may vary with the family member.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Apply EP Proposition 3.1 to the restriction-of-scalars integral group scheme, with connected split reductive generic fibre.
For a stable lattice Θ in nonzero W, untwist the diagonal action on O[[H]]⊗_OΘ to identify it with a positive finite direct sum of O[[H]].
The Hom–tensor adjunction and capture of projectives detect the original quotient; positivity of dim W is essential. Extend coefficients member by member using EP §2.3.
acceptance: W=0 is excluded: zero testing representations cannot capture O[[K]].
No admissibility of Π(M∞) is assumed; compact projectivity suffices.

nodes.title: Capture by smooth types
nodes.statement: Use the type-theory supplier for the EP families: principal-series Vχ on a sufficiently small torsion-free Iwahori subgroup I_{n0}, and minimal-stratum V(α,θ) on H=U^{m+1}(𝔄) for an embedded degree-d extension E/F containing a minimal element, m sufficiently large that H is torsion free. In the principal family characters have pairwise separated conductors as in EP §3.3; in the supercuspidal family take all distinct isomorphism classes for all n>2m, v_E(α)=−n and θ∈C(m,α). Each family captures every compact projective over its H. Tensoring it with the nonzero fixed algebraic factor πalg(k)|_H preserves capture.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Import the actual induced representations, hereditary-order filtration and simple-character intertwiners from the requested smooth-representation interface.

Use EP Proposition 2.23: for the p-power-compatible filtration H_n and pairwise nonisomorphic absolutely irreducible V_i, the growth Σ_i(dim V_i^{H_n})²∼[H:H_n] implies capture. Here ∼ means bounded above and below by positive constants, as used in EP.
Principal-series counts are EP Lemma 3.10 and Proposition 3.11; simple-type dimensions and counts are Lemma 3.20 and Proposition 3.25, giving Proposition 3.26.
Apply nonzero tensor stability to πalg(k). Restriction of the parent projective module to finite-index H remains projective.
acceptance: Counting the same irreducible representation repeatedly cannot replace the sum over distinct isomorphism classes.
Use the p-power-compatible filtration in EP Proposition 2.23; an arbitrary filtration has no such growth theorem.

nodes.title: Fixed-centre algebraic density
nodes.statement: Let 𝐆/Q_p be connected reductive and split over L, Z its centre and H⊆𝐆(Q_p) compact open. Let T≠0 be a finite-dimensional algebraic L-representation whose central character restricts to δ:H∩Z(Q_p)→O×. If Π is an admissible unitary Banach representation that is a continuous H-equivariant direct summand of Cδ(H,L)^m, m≥1, then the images of Hom_H(T⊗ξ′,Π^la)⊗(T⊗ξ′), for ξ′ irreducible algebraic representations of (𝐆/Z)_L, span a dense subspace of Π^la. They also span a dense subspace of Π, using density of locally analytic vectors in an admissible Banach representation. All analytic vectors here are locally Q_p-analytic.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Use DPS Theorem 7.4 and Corollaries 7.5–7.6 for algebraic matrix coefficients on the compact open of the quotient by the centre.
Tensor by T*; the projection formula Cδ(H,L)⊗T*≅C(H/(H∩Z),L)^{dim T} removes the central character. Pass to the continuous direct summand.
Apply DPS Corollary 7.8 for density in Π^la. The requested LR.1 Banach analytic-vector-density interface gives density in Π; this additional implication is explicit.
acceptance: A nonzero bounded projection from Cδ(H,L)^m detects at least one algebraic summand.
The theorem is not applied directly to Π(M∞), which need not be admissible.

nodes.title: Algebraic detection of projectives
nodes.statement: For K=GL_d(O_F), let θ be an algebraic character of (Res_{F/Q_p}G_m)_L, with evaluation δ on Z∩K. If M is a nonzero projective in the category of compact O[[K]]-modules on which Z∩K acts by δ^{-1}, then Hom_cont,K(M,ξ*)≠0 for some irreducible algebraic ξ of (Res_{F/Q_p}GL_d)_L.

proofSteps: A compact fixed-centre projective is a product of indecomposable projectives. A nonzero factor is a summand of the fixed-centre completed regular module; its Banach dual is a nonzero summand of Cδ(K,L).

nodes.title: Detection of local components
nodes.statement: For every minimal prime 𝔭χ of R=R□_{ρ̄}, there is a minimal prime 𝔮 of R∞ with 𝔮∩R=𝔭χ and V(𝔮)⊆V(Ann_{R∞}M∞). More precisely, a crystalline determinant ψ restricting to χ on μ_{p∞}(F) and some algebraic ξ give a nonzero characteristic-zero fixed-ψ fibre of M∞(ξ); a point y of that fibre lies on such a component V(𝔮). No containment of the entire support of M∞(ξ) in one component is asserted.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: For the chosen χ, import the corrected crystalline-character lift interface to choose ψ lifting detρ̄ and realizing χ.

The nonzero fixed-centre projective Mψ has an algebraic test ξ by PD.2. Duality gives a nonzero fixed-ψ rational testing module. Its finite presentation over a characteristic-zero quotient of R∞ gives a closed point y.

Every algebraic test is annihilated by Ann_{R∞}M∞, so y∈V(Ann M∞). The parent EP support theorem makes this closed set a union of irreducible components. Choose one such component through y; the algebraic-test closure form of EP Theorem 6.12 gives the same argument.

At y, p is invertible; distinct determinant-torsion characters have distinct values, so its χ-component is unique. The component bijection of PD.1 forces 𝔮∩R=𝔭χ. This repairs the whole-support containment step in the printed proof.

nodes.title: Density from patched testing
nodes.statement: Let R→R∞ act on the imported compact projective M∞, faithfully over R. Let (V_i) capture M∞ on a fixed compact open H⊆K, and let N_i=M∞,H(Θ_i) be the finite integral tests. Suppose each B_i=R∞/Ann_{R∞}N_i is reduced and O-flat (the zero ring is allowed), and the image in Spec R of every closed point of Spec B_i[1/p] lies in a set Σ of arithmetic points. Then the vanishing ideal of Σ in R is zero and Σ is Zariski dense in Spec R. More generally, without local faithfulness its closure is V(Ann_R M∞) if, in addition, Σ⊆V(Ann_R M∞).
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: A scalar vanishing on Σ vanishes on every characteristic-zero closed point of B_i. Its generic fibre is Jacobson with finite residue extensions; reducedness and O-flatness give that the scalar is zero in B_i.
Thus it kills N_i, hence kills every testing map by the dual-Hom comparison. Capture says its endomorphism on M∞ is zero.
Capture gives vanishingIdeal(Σ)⊆Ann_R M∞. If Σ⊆V(Ann_R M∞), the reverse inclusion also holds; in the faithful case both are zero. Baseline zero-locus/closure gives the conclusion.
This argument takes finite tests over R∞; it never assumes that M∞ is finite over R[[H]]. Equivalently EP Proposition 2.11 may be applied to R∞/Ann M∞ and then contracted.
acceptance: Without reducedness, the proof only detects a radical; a uniform nilpotence bound is the more general EP hypothesis.
The zero test imposes no points and has zero faithful quotient.
The result is scheme-theoretic Zariski density in Spec R, not density in a Banach topology.

nodes.title: Benign crystalline points
nodes.statement: A crystalline representation of G_F with regular labelled weights is benign when (i) its φ^f eigenvalues on Dcris, after splitting coefficients, are pairwise distinct; (ii) every ordering of those eigenlines gives a noncritical refinement, in the sense imported from the refined crystalline space; and (iii) for distinct eigenvalues α_i,α_j one has α_i/α_j≠p^f and p^{−f}. Here f=[F_0:Q_p]. A benign point is an arithmetic point with this property, and its weights may vary.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Use the imported Dcris, labelled filtrations and refinement construction. Require all d! refinements to be noncritical, not just one.
The predicate is invariant under a splitting-field extension and eigenvalue permutation, so it descends to arithmetic points.
The spectral ratio restriction is additional to regularity and noncriticality; it ensures irreducibility of the associated unramified principal series.
acceptance: Use φ^f, which is linear on each F_0-component, rather than treating the semilinear φ as an ordinary matrix.

nodes.title: Prescribed-type support
nodes.statement: Let τ be a compatible inertial type and W=σ(τ) a specified finite-dimensional smooth crystalline K-type over a finite extension of L, with the CEGGPS N=0 recognition theorem. For each algebraic ξ let N_{ξ,τ}=M∞(ξ⊗W) using its integral stable lattice for annihilators, and put Jτ=⋂_ξ Ann_R N_{ξ,τ}, Cτ=V(Jτ)⊆Spec R. Define Στ to be the potentially crystalline arithmetic points of inertial type τ and arbitrary regular weight, and Στ^patch to be images of the characteristic-zero closed points of the faithful quotients of the tests. Their type recognition is part of the specified datum. Nonempty type support means at least one rational N_{ξ,τ} is nonzero. For a degenerate testing datum W=0 take Jτ=R and Cτ=∅.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Build the tests using the specified smooth K-type, not merely a name for τ. Contract each finite-test annihilator from R∞ to R before intersecting.
Use parent reduced O-flat faithful type quotients to see that Jτ is radical and p-saturated. Their characteristic-zero closed-point images have vanishing ideal Jτ.
Compare their points with potentially crystalline N=0 deformations using the requested inertial local Langlands interface. No type is inferred just from potentially semistable membership.

nodes.statement: Fix an embedded extension E/F of degree d containing an element minimal over F. Write e=e(E/F), v_E normalized and ϖ_F a uniformizer. Minimal means gcd(e,v_E(α))=1 and the residue of ϖ_F^{−v_E(α)}α^e generates k_E/k_F. Let 𝔄 be the hereditary order of End_F(E) preserving the chain (𝔭_E^i). For regular weight k, Σsc_{k,E} consists of potentially semistable points of that weight whose local Langlands representation is supercuspidal and contains a simple stratum [𝔄,n,0,α] with F[α]=E and α minimal, v_E(α)=−n<0. Simple strata, simple characters and their occurrence are imported from the smooth-representation owner. No induced-character description is imposed for wild E/F.
hypotheses: Standing arithmetic setup of PD.0; p does not divide 2d for every assertion using M∞.
proofSteps: Apply the supplied minimal-stratum/type occurrence predicate to the local Langlands representation. The field embedding and lattice chain are specified up to conjugacy.
The numerical minimality condition is the EP §3.4 input; it implies F[α]=E. The filtration and type constructors remain the supplier’s definitions.
Use type recognition to see that such supercuspidal points have N=0. Character induction is available only under the extra tame hypothesis of EP Proposition 3.19.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.8, p. 49, published 2023 PDF
sourceIssues.printed: From the closure of a union of algebraic test supports being a union of components, the proof places the entire support of one chosen test inside a single irreducible component.
sourceIssues.correction: Choose a characteristic-zero point y of its nonzero fixed-ψ fibre and then choose a component of V(Ann M∞) through y, using the imported EP support theorem. The uniqueness of the χ-component at y gives the needed contraction. No whole-support containment is needed.
sourceIssues.reason: A subset of a union of components can meet more than one component; for example Spec L[x,y]/(xy) itself is not contained in either component. The stated union conclusion alone does not justify the stronger containment. The component-through-y argument proves the theorem with the available inputs.
